outcome: Identify ferrous and non-ferrous metals and alloys by appearance and by toughness, ductility, malleability, hardness and strength.
Explain how metal properties change through alloying, grain size, cold working, hardening, quenching, corrosion and carbon content.
Identify thermoplastics (ABS, acrylic, nylon, polycarbonate, polystyrene) and thermosets (epoxy, resins, polyurethane, vulcanised rubber).
Explain the effects of heat on thermosets and thermoplastics.
Identify composites: carbon-fibre, GRP, plywood, MDF, OSB and structural concrete.
Explain how reinforcement direction, matrix, amount, size and shape change a composite's properties.
Identify structural timbers and ceramics, and describe their properties.
Compare the cost, availability, form and supply of engineering materials, with at least three examples.
Calculate manufacturing costs using stock sizes, price breaks from economies of scale, and waste.
Explain whether materials can be machined, treated, shaped and recycled.
Weigh the benefits, drawbacks and environmental impact of wind, solar, tidal, nuclear, fossil fuel and biomass energy.
Explain engineered lifespans: planned obsolescence, sealed parts and maintenance needs.
Explain why products need maintenance (safety, efficiency, lubrication, corrosion, wear, end of life) and how statistics predict service intervals.
Explain how material availability and forms affect cost, and how user requirements affect material and process choice.
Describe fused deposition, sintering for metals and rapid prototyping for polymers.
Describe cutting by sawing, shearing and laser, and calculate cutting speeds.
Describe cylindrical and tapered turning and boring, and calculate angles.
Describe face and slot milling.
Use pillar drill and lathe centre drilling, and select spindle speeds.
Describe chemical etching for PCB manufacture.
Describe forming and manipulation by bending, folding, press forming, composite lay up, punching and stamping, with related calculations.
Describe pressure die casting, sand casting and injection moulding.
Choose permanent and temporary joining methods: rivets, threaded fastenings, soldering, brazing and welding.
Describe normalising, annealing, hardening and quenching.
Describe painting, dip coating, electroplating, galvanising and polishing.
Describe systems and sub-systems with block diagrams, schematics and flow charts.
Explain linkages and conversion of motion, such as rotary to reciprocating.
Explain gear trains, chains and sprockets, and calculate gear ratio and mechanical advantage.
Explain cams and followers, including cams in engines.
Explain how pulleys reduce effort or transfer power, and the role of bearings.
Describe power supplies, input control devices (relays, switches) and output devices (motors, buzzers, bells, lamps, solenoids).
State the difference between alternating and direct current.
Describe electronic inputs such as light and temperature sensors, and analogue and digital signals.
Describe process devices: timers, counters, comparators and AND, OR, NOT logic.
Explain microcontrollers (PIC) replacing discrete process circuits.
Explain driver components such as transistors and FETs, and analogue to digital conversion.
Describe output components: LEDs, 7 segment displays, buzzers and piezo sounders.
Describe resistors, diodes and capacitors within a circuit.
Use flow charts for simple programs controlling up to three inputs and three outputs.
Explain how static, dynamic and imposed loads act, including space frames and monocoques, causing bending, torsion and buckling.
Explain the uses of, and differences between, pneumatic and hydraulic circuits with examples.
Predict system performance with calculations, simulation and CAD modelling of circuits and fluid forces.
Calculate area, volume, stiffness, density, Young's modulus and factors of safety.
Calculate forces, stress and strain from load and extension, and resistance, current and voltage.
Test materials and structures under load, including tensile and compressive strength.
Explain destructive and non-destructive testing and their advantages.
Test and modify control programs, for example changing motor speed or sensor thresholds.
Apply quality control checks and tolerances during production.
Explain lift, drag and thrust with an example.
Discuss with examples how new technologies affect production, society and the environment.
Discuss positive and negative impacts of engineering industries on social and economic infrastructure.
Solve problems logically and analyse existing solutions, using block diagrams and flowcharts.
Produce engineering drawings: third-angle orthographic, isometric, assembly and section views.
Use 2D and 3D CAD to create a solution.
Use CNC and CAM such as laser cutting, vinyl cutting, PCB routing and turning.
Test materials under load, and produce and follow a production plan covering materials, processes, time and safety.
Predict performance with calculations and iconic, analogue or symbolic models.
Safely select and use materials, parts, components, tools and equipment, and processes such as marking, turning, milling and joining.
Apply quality control, working to tolerances and checking with Vernier calipers, micrometers and depth gauges.
Design tests of fitness for purpose and identify improvements.
